mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is a negative predictor of S&P 500 forward returns, indicating restrictive monetary policy compresses equity valuation multiples and leads to negative 20-day returns regardless of economic context.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is observed, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.5% signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 2.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicate a tightening monetary policy cycle with rising inflation, compressing equity valuation multiples and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are both rising, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by GDP growth rate > 2.5% and unemployment rate < 4.5%), the S&P 500 is expected to have negative forward returns due to overvaluation and reduced policy margin for error.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth > 2.5% and UNRATE < 4.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger central bank rate cuts, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 2200 units signal a strong housing market indicating robust economic growth and positive equity market sentiment, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST > 2200, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 115 (2017=100) signals an economic slowdown that triggers central bank rate cuts, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 115, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in private employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signal a strong labor market that reduces recession risk and supports positive equity market sentiment, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 0.5% m/m and UNRATE < 0.3% m/m, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
